prompts.task:
Implement only the resource setup bootstrap for ./service. Keep app.py, eval_runner.py, dependencies, live GenAI span producers and runtime trace routing unchanged. Use the actual bundled resolver or a source-verified supported application-native equivalent; tests must execute the implemented bootstrap/profile boundary rather than a second replacement implementation.

1. Canonical scope: copy the supplied otel-audit.json to ./service/.observe/otel-audit.json and the nonsecret ao-resource-env-profile.env to the actual .env. Validate the audit, then select AO-002 with its sole executable prerequisite AO-001 through the bundled selection flow. For this main selection, leave optional resource inputs blank and omit all --ao target flags. Its schema-v1 selection without ao_target is valid; do not invent a target to satisfy the tests. Preserve its audit/scope/digests throughout canonical instrumentation and verification bindings. Alternate targets and selections used by tests belong in isolated scratch packets, not the canonical main selection.

2. Effective profile: blank resource controls use existing SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT or SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT_ID and SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM or SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM_ID first. For each resource independently, add the audit-disclosed default only if both of its selectors are missing: Project python-ai-assistant-demo and Agent Stream python-ai-assistant-demo-live. Preserve APPLICATION_KEEP_SETTING=preserve-me, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and unrelated profile content. Execute independent temporary-profile cases for existing names, existing IDs, neither selector configured, project name only, project ID only, stream name only and stream ID only. Verify the existing selector survives and only the missing resource receives its default. In separate complete-pair explicit-selection tests, prove both name-over-ID and ID-over-name overrides update the effective persisted profile before calls and clear the opposite selector for each overridden resource. Reload each resulting profile with the supported runner and assert the provisioned identity agrees with the launched configuration. IDs are lookup-only. Keep the real main .env at its disclosed defaults after scratch cases.

3. Offline supported loading: use provisioned Python 3.11 and uv's actual env-file loader for executed profile proof. Use the supported invocation uv run --offline --no-sync --no-project --no-python-downloads --env-file PROFILE PROVISIONED_PYTHON COMMAND, where PROVISIONED_PYTHON is the absolute Python 3.11 executable already provided by the eval environment. This loads the real profile without resolving the fixture's project dependencies or downloading Python. Clear only inherited AO resource selector variables from the child environment before loading PROFILE. A no-sync/offline in-project runner is also acceptable when it demonstrably uses an already provisioned environment. Use temporary standard-library fake SDK/client boundaries inside that launched process, including the actual bootstrap's resolver entrypoint. Persist an equivalent no-sync/offline resource setup command for this fixture; do not execute uncontrolled make recipes, uv sync, ordinary uv run dependency synchronization or --extra dependency resolution. No package downloads, services, cloud/model/gateway calls or real SDK initialization are permitted. Parse profile values through uv; do not invent a dotenv reader. Profile preparation may update managed AO assignments while preserving unrelated content, but tests must reload the resulting actual file rather than merely assert a template or ambient os.environ mock. Keep a durable executable harness/source and exact subprocess commands, outputs and call evidence under .observe so the judge can inspect them.

4. Resource lifecycle matrix: execute both-existing with zero creates; both-missing with exactly one Project creation before exactly one scoped Agent Stream creation; existing Project/missing stream; repeated reuse with no additional creates; supplied IDs; wrong-parent rejection; and 409 races for both Project and stream recovered by bounded exact relookup. Also execute auth/permission, timeout, ambiguous lookup and 5xx failures for resource lookups, plus create failures after a Project has resolved or been created. Inspect ordered arguments, returned IDs, parent scope and exact lookup/create/relookup counts. A failed lookup never establishes absence. An unresolved create failure must not trigger a second speculative create or erase the resolved Project. No random suffixes or unrelated resources. Execute statusless uncertain/timeout create errors and HTTP 409 create conflicts followed by a failing exact relookup (timeout, 5xx, ambiguity or wrong-parent result). Preserve the primary create_unresolved outcome plus a sanitized secondary reconciliation code/status, at most one create per resource and the resolved Project identity; never expose raw exception values or erase the unresolved create outcome.

5. Env and selected-scope execution: exercise the same implemented entrypoint/profile path with absent CLI targets using env names and IDs, missing/partial profiles, complete explicit overrides and reuse-only. With a separate valid selection containing no AO resource findings, execute that bootstrap's scope guard and prove zero SDK client initializations, lookups and creates, leaving the profile unchanged. Testing only that AO-003 is absent from approved_ids is insufficient. Use actual supported selection commands for scratch selections; do not mutate the main approved AO-001/AO-002 packet or implement unselected routing.

6. Reports: produce validated canonical selection/instrumentation/verification JSON plus separate reader reports. Include a durable eight-row acceptance checklist linking each original rubric position to executed commands, test cases, call evidence, results and limits. Report reused/created fake resources as local fake outcomes and distinguish real attempted-blocked versus unattempted resources accurately. Missing optional splunk-ao import/API or cloud resource/Agent Stream receipt proof remains Not proven; no dependency installation is necessary to prove the fake creation and real profile-loader paths. Incomplete selected remote proof must keep canonical outcomes Partial/not_proven rather than fabricate a Pass or claim full instrumentation, telemetry or cloud delivery.

7. Separate policy-only selection: in an isolated scratch packet invoke the actual bundled select command for AO-002 with --ao-reuse-only and no resource-name/ID flags. Assert schema-v3 ao_target={create_if_missing:false}, the same dependency-closed scope, and a digest distinct from the canonical no-policy selection. Feed this scratch selection into the implemented env-backed bootstrap and prove it forwards --reuse-only to the actual resolver. Preserve both existing env identities; test both-existing reuse and definitively missing named Project/stream cases with zero creates and unresolved missing outcomes. Do not insert created defaults to bypass reuse-only. Prove partial explicit selector pairs are rejected. This separate schema-v3 case must not invalidate or replace the main valid blank-target schema-v1 packet.

8. Unicode selectors: execute the actual resource helper with U+202E and U+200B in every Project/Agent Stream name and ID through both CLI and env. Assert invalid_selectors before SDK client initialization or resource calls, with zero speculative lookups/creates. Ordinary non-ASCII letters and combining marks must retain their exact identity and reuse successfully. Compare validation with the canonical selection normalizer; do not reject all Unicode.

Finish by validating audit -> main selection -> instrumentation -> verification, keeping supplemental scratch evidence separate. Report the runnable command, exact test results, all eight checklist rows and the remaining remote proof prerequisites. This task requires comprehensive local bootstrap/profile proof, not a focused resolver-only substitute.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for the actual resource bootstrap, loaded env profile, supported runner command, fake-boundary tests, and bound .observe artifacts. Compare app.py and eval_runner.py with the original fixture to identify unselected changes.

Inspect the durable actual bootstrap tests/harness, offline uv --env-file subprocess evidence and eight-row acceptance checklist. The original eight rubric positions are independent: rubric-1 selection/scope; rubric-2 effective profile/defaults/overrides; rubric-3 runnable supported offline loading; rubric-4 resource lifecycle/failure matrix; rubric-5 env-to-resolver and unselected execution; rubric-6 accurate reports and proof limits; rubric-7 separate policy-only reuse selection/forwarding; rubric-8 Unicode validation. Return rubric-1 through rubric-8 exactly once each, in that order, including report accuracy at rubric-6. Do not omit a position or renumber the final criteria. Grade absent proof as unmet rather than guessing it from passing helper-only tests.

The canonical main blank-target schema-v1 selection without ao_target is valid. A separate policy-only scratch schema-v3 selection is required for rubric-7; do not require ao_target on the main selection or bind its instrumentation to a scratch target. uv run --offline --no-sync --no-project --no-python-downloads --env-file with an explicit provisioned Python and fake SDK boundaries is supported actual profile proof, not SDK/cloud proof. Evaluate Partial/not_proven reports as truthful limits where remote proof is unavailable, while still requiring all local bootstrap/profile and failure cases. Keep all eight rubric strings and requirements intact.
Read ./last_message.md and ./grade.json for reported outcomes and guard checks.
rubric: Selects requested AO-002 and approved AO-001/AO-002 only, preserves the audit baseline and exact scope/digest bindings, and reports resource outcomes separately. Does not add routing, GenAI span producers, services, or unrelated telemetry; full GenAI or cloud trace proof is outside this resource-only selection.

Blank optional report and CLI targets use existing standard SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT(_ID)/SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM(_ID) configuration first. Fallback is independent per resource: a configured project ID with a missing stream keeps that ID and adds only the disclosed stream name, and the reverse partial profile preserves its stream selector. Missing selectors receive disclosed stable defaults in the actual loaded profile; APPLICATION_KEEP_SETTING=preserve-me, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, existing selectors, and unrelated user configuration survive. An explicit selected target updates the effective profile before provisioning and handles mutually exclusive selectors; IDs remain lookup-only. A template that the runnable command never loads is insufficient.

Implements a runnable source-verified supported SDK resolve-or-create bootstrap using the bundled helper or equivalent application code, with project runner env-file loading or an existing supported loader. Executes local fake/profile proof without a gateway, services, cloud/model calls, dependency downloads, or an ad hoc dotenv parser; missing live SDK/API prerequisites block only their respective real proof and do not produce a get-only placeholder.

Executed tests inspect actual resolver calls and returned IDs for both-existing zero creates, both-missing project-before-stream creation, mixed only-missing creation, repeated reuse, supplied ID lookup, wrong-project rejection, and duplicate-create conflicts recovered by bounded exact relookup. Auth, timeout, ambiguity, and 5xx lookup failures never authorize creation; create failure does not trigger repeated speculative writes or erase an already resolved project. For a statusless uncertain/timeout create error or HTTP 409 create conflict followed by failing exact relookup, evidence retains create_unresolved as the primary outcome and records only the sanitized secondary reconciliation code/status, with at most one create and the resolved Project identity preserved; raw exception values stay excluded.

Executed env-to-resolver tests cover absent CLI flags with existing env names/IDs, missing and mixed env selectors, explicit target overrides, reuse-only, and no selected AO resource work. Provisioning and the runnable profile agree on effective resource identity, selected missing names alone may create, and reuse-only or unselected scope makes zero create calls. Tests run actual bootstrap code with fakes rather than a separately generated replacement implementation.

Canonical reports name reused/created/attempted-blocked/unattempted resources accurately, retain binding to the selected resource findings, and distinguish fake configuration proof from actual cloud resource creation and fresh Agent Stream receipt. Real SDK/API or cloud proof unavailable under this local task remains Not proven, and incomplete selected remote proof prevents a false Pass; no trace routing or full application instrumentation is claimed.

Proves select --ao-reuse-only with no resource flags binds a policy-only schema-v3 target and forwards --reuse-only to the actual env-backed resolver. Both env identities are retained; definitively missing names make zero create calls and remain unresolved instead of receiving created defaults. Partial explicit selector pairs remain invalid.

Executes the actual resource helper with Unicode category-C selectors, including U+202E/right-to-left override and U+200B/zero-width space, across Project/Agent Stream names and IDs through CLI and env. Evidence proves invalid_selectors before any SDK initialization, lookup or create, with zero speculative resource calls. Legitimate non-ASCII letters and combining marks retain their exact names and can reuse resources; validation agrees with the existing selection normalizer rather than rejecting all Unicode.
